messages.text: I recorded this explanation in OBS today. Please turn the recordings in raw/ into one focused portrait educational short for YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and TikTok. Choose a clear takeaway that stands on its own, removing failed starts, repetition, and unnecessary dead time. Use the project's light/dark monochrome visual style, improve the voice with local AI cleanup, and add explanatory motion graphics where they make the idea easier to follow. Use the screen and camera footage appropriately. Deliver one finished 1080 × 1920 video with readable captions positioned for the three platforms, timed caption files, and an editable project here for me to review. Don't post it to any social platform.

I’ll review the recordings, choose a self-contained takeaway, and build a portrait edit with cleaned voice, captions, and supporting graphics. I’m using the video editing, video review, motion graphics, and writing skills for this project.

The camera footage is usable, but the separate screen recording is distorted throughout. The OBS program recording has a clean view of the screen, so I can use that as the fallback. I’m checking the speech and audio tracks before choosing the cut.

I’ve found the strongest takeaway: don’t give one AI agent access to private data, untrusted content, and the ability to send information out. I’m shaping a roughly 50-second short around that risk and your email workflow example, with a diagram that separates the agent’s job from drafting and human approval.

The cut now runs about 47 seconds. I’ve removed the restarts and kept the warning, the three permissions, and the practical email example. The graphics will sit above a prominent camera view, with captions in a fixed lane near the seam. Voice cleanup is running locally with DeepFilterNet 3.

The layout is ready for review: the original screen diagram briefly introduces the framework, then the animation shows the three permissions and the separate email workflow. I’m checking the captioned preview for framing, cut timing, and text collisions before the full-quality export.

The preview reads well at portrait size. I found two brief overlaps during diagram transitions and adjusted them. The speech check also caught a cut that was too close to the start of “So,” so I’m restoring that word before exporting.

The full-resolution export is finished. I’m checking the encoded files for decode errors, loudness, caption timing, and the final frames. The handoff will include the captioned short, a clean master, SRT/VTT files, editable sources, and a local review page with a voice-cleanup comparison.

Both versions passed full decode checks. The encoded voice measures −16.8 LUFS with a −1.69 dBTP peak. The finished short is 44.9 seconds; I’m packaging the project and review notes, including the listening checks and platform draft previews that still need human review.

Created a **44.9-second, 1080 × 1920 short** about separating AI-agent permissions, with local AI voice cleanup, monochrome animation, and captions.
